description: Beating #1 (27023, =2.08x over stock 56238 baseline) by 20% REQUIRES ~2x on the dense cond2 shapes 3/4/6/7 + dense-even 11 (n=512/1024 b640/b60), which 4 workers refuted via one-CTA-per-matrix (cuSOLVER wins by keeping each matrix L2-resident; batched one-CTA blows L2 -> symv bandwidth floor). The ONE untapped lever: EMULATED-FP32 tensor-core GEMM (per environment.md, cuBLAS bf16x9 emulation = ~FP32-accurate at up to ~3x native FP32). It bridges the exact wall that killed briefs 1/3/4: bf16 reduction gave eig~3000 (inaccurate), FP32 SIMT was accurate but slow. FIRST probe torch's fp32-precision/emulation knob (torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision='tf32'/'bf16x3'/'ieee', or set_float32_matmul_precision) AND a hand-rolled bf16x3 split (A=hi+lo bf16, 3 TC GEMMs) on B200 -- measure GEMM accuracy+speed vs FP32 SIMT and bf16. THEN build a two-stage dense->band reduction whose trailing two-sided update is ONE emulated-FP32 batched GEMM (syr2k) across ALL matrices at once (compute-bound, fills GPU, avoids the per-column symv L2 floor); band->tridiag on the narrow band; reuse brief-1's banked 3ms SMEM bisection + brief-3's WY back-transform. Fix the eig~3000 two-stage accuracy bug brief-4 hit (likely QR-panel/band-tridiag reflector composition, not precision). Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; route n=512/1024 dense. Forks best 9d38abc2 so it STACKS with n=352. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 45475 + 39/39 idle-verified.

t1: two-stage TF32 dense->band->tridiag, routed dense n=512/1024. CORRECT (39/39, reflector composition verified FP64 ||AQ-QL||~5e-15 -- fixes brief-4 eig~3000 bug). Stage1 dense->band=batched qr_panel kernel (replaces serial cuSOLVER geqrf 73->4ms/panel) + trailing two-sided ONE batched TF32 GEMM (9ms total b640 n512 -- the emulated-FP32 lever WORKS). Stage2 chase stores reflectors; stage-2 backtransform=column-parallel bt_apply. geomean 95400 (regression vs 45522). b640 n512 breakdown: stage1 61 + chase 216 + solve 48 + bt_apply 131 = 478ms vs cuSOLVER 171. The two O(n^3) SIMT pieces (chase, bt_apply) are the wall; n=1024 6x worse (n^3 scaling). TF32 GEMM reduction+tail cheap.

t2: SMEM-resident chase + bw=12, route ONLY n=512 dense (n=1024 band 508KB overflows SMEM -> stays cuSOLVER, undoing t1's 6x n=1024 regression). Validates 39/39. geomean 60089 (t1 was 95400; parent 45522). n=512 dense (3/6/8/11) ~423-451ms vs cuSOLVER 165-203ms (2.5x). b640 n512: stage1 58 + chase 129 + solve 48 + bt_apply 126. WALLS measured: chase latency-bound sequential (41ms b<=296 -> 129ms b640, SMEM-limited occupancy); bt_apply O(n^3) SIMT (needs tensor-core WY-blocking); tail already ~130ms near cuSOLVER 171ms. Emulated-FP32 GEMM probe: torch 2.12 has NO bf16x9; hand-rolled bf16x3=0.67-1.1x FP32 (loss); TF32=8.8x FP32 at relerr 2.9e-4 = the real lever (stage-1 trailing GEMM 9ms).

t3: batch-adaptive chase (global chase at b640=102ms beats SMEM 129ms due to occupancy; SMEM wins b<=296=43ms). geomean 58956 (t2 60089). n=512 dense 3/6/8/11 ~395-422ms vs cuSOLVER 165-203ms. Still regresses; walls unchanged (bt_apply 126ms O(n^3) SIMT + chase sequential; tail ~120ms already near cuSOLVER 171).

BUILT + measured the full two-stage EMULATED-FP32 dense->band->tridiag eigensolver (3 trials, HEAD=453cb8d7, geomean 58956 vs parent 45522 -- a REGRESSION, so the manager keeps 9d38abc2 as best). It VALIDATES 39/39 and is a bankable, correct asset. Key measured results the manager should weigh before deciding whether to invest further:

EMULATED-FP32 GEMM PROBE (brief step 1, done first): torch 2.12 exposes NO cuBLAS bf16x9/bf16x3 for matmul (fp32_precision only accepts 'ieee'/'tf32'; mixing it with the legacy allow_tf32 API errors). Hand-rolled bf16x3 split (A=hi+lo bf16, 3 bmms) = 0.67-1.1x FP32 (a LOSS -- the 3 bf16 bmms+casts cost more than one TF32 pass). **TF32 IS the emulated-FP32 lever here: 8.8-10.3x FP32-SIMT (523-656 TFLOPS) at relerr 2.9e-4** -- plenty for the loose eigh gate. The brief's premise (bf16x9 emulation) is not reachable in torch 2.12; TF32 is the substitute and it works.

THE TWO-STAGE WORKS + FIXES brief-4's BUG: reflector composition Q=Q1(Q2 V_tri) verified to FP64 (||AQ-QL||~5e-15 on n<=96 reference). Stage 1 dense->band(bw): batched panel-QR kernel (replaces cuSOLVER geqrf which SERIALIZES per-matrix = 73ms->4ms/panel) + trailing two-sided update as ONE batched TF32 GEMM (only 9ms for n=512 b640 -- the lever fills the GPU as promised). Stage 2 chase stores reflectors (band-restricted, SMEM-resident where it fits). Solve = brief-1's SMEM Sturm-bisection.

THE WALLS (why it regresses, all measured idle at n=512 b640, cuSOLVER=171ms):
- FULL two-stage (bw=12, best) = 396ms. Breakdown: stage1 87 + chase(global) 101 + bt_apply 116 + solve/finalize 92.
- bt_apply (stage-2 eigenvector back-transform) = 116ms, O(n^3) SIMT. It MUST be tensor-core (WY-blocked) to be cheap.
- chase (band->tridiag) = 101ms at b640 (global; memory-throughput-bound floor). SMEM chase is 43ms at b<=296 but occupancy-throttled to 129ms at b640 (100KB band caps concurrent CTAs). This is the harder wall -- it's sequential and memory-bound.
- CRITICAL: even bt_apply->0 leaves chase 101 + tail(stage1+solve+finalize ~200, ~120 after slimming) which ALREADY meets/exceeds cuSOLVER 171ms. So the pipeline is at-best-break-even, extending brief-1's Householder-mechanism finding to the two-stage case.
- FUNDAMENTAL TENSION (measured): the chase wants SMALL bw (chase ~ n^2*bw/2; bw=12 best full-pipeline) but a tensor-core bt_apply wants LARGE bw (fewer reflectors: R~n^2/2bw -> fewer WY panels). Neither bw wins: bw=12 FULL=396ms, bw=32 FULL=481ms.
- n=1024: band (508KB) overflows SMEM; two-stage = 527ms vs cuSOLVER 106ms (5x, O(n^3) bt_apply dominates). Left on cuSOLVER (trials 2/3 route only n=512).
- Some stage-1 two-sided GEMMs run as SIMT sgemm not tensorop (~38ms) because bw=12 (K-dim) isn't 8-aligned; bw=16/24/32 route them to tensorop but the chase penalty outweighs it.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (unbuilt, surfaced for the manager -- a win needs SEVERAL of these together and the ROI is a marginal ~4% n=512 win at best):
1. TENSOR-CORE WY bt_apply (brief's explicit 'reuse brief-3 WY' ask): the stage-2 chase reflectors within ONE sweep are DISJOINT (tile the rows in bw-blocks -> T is diagonal, 2 GEMMs/sweep, exact). But n sweeps = too many launches; batching sweep-blocks needs the compact-WY-with-overlap T (staggered supports) -- a real SBR back-transform build (large, high correctness risk). Biggest single lever (116->~15-50ms) but bw-tension caps the net.
2. A GEMM-based or multi-CTA-per-matrix band->tridiag to break the chase's sequential/memory floor (101ms). The chase is the binding wall; without it a win is impossible.
3. FUSED band-solver megakernel: feed the bw=24 band (packed ~25KB) to a band-aware version of the parent's mega_eigh_med (fused tridiag+bisect+twisted+WY-backtransform in SMEM, one CTA/matrix) -- reuses the proven n<=448 megakernel machinery and eliminates the chase + bt_apply global traffic. OVERLAPS brief-3's fused-megakernel territory -> a coordinated brief. Most promising structural departure.
4. Tail fusion: stage1 has ~49ms non-GEMM overhead (qr_panel+T-loop); fuse qr+T+trailing-update. Solve/finalize ~92ms (twisted 2.5ms + FP32 ortho/gate GEMMs) -- slim the FP32 ortho.

Banked assets on this branch (correct, reusable): batched qr_panel kernel, TF32 dense->band stage, SMEM+global bulge-chase kernels (store reflectors), column-parallel bt_apply, and the FP64-verified composition. The protected shapes (n=176/352/clustered/geometric) are UNTOUCHED (routing gates n=512 dense only).
